title: Onboard telemetry exporter and autodraft release briefs
author: Priya Rao
description: Add a lightweight telemetry exporter for onboarding flows and an autodraft release-brief generator that synthesizes profile diffs, provenance, and performance highlights into a concise release note draft. Motivation: onboarding teams frequently ask for a quick artifact that explains what changed between model versions, the observable perf regressions/improvements, and where the raw telemetry is stored. This PR introduces a streaming exporter (JSONL to object store), a compact release brief synthesizer that consumes profile diffs and sampled traces, and a small UI hook that surfaces the autodraft in the model registry review flow. Checklist: [x] export telemetry (JSONL) with schema v1; [x] profile diff producer and sampler; [x] autodraft generator that emits markdown summary; [x] UI hook in onboard review to preview the draft; [x] tests for exporter and synthesizer; [x] docs and quickstart. Key constraints and decisions: exporter is append-only and writes per-model per-version shards to the configured storage URI to avoid locking; the autodraft runs as a post-onboard job and is idempotent; we keep the schema minimal (timestamp,event_type,route,seq_len,latency_ms,hash) to avoid leaking PII and to remain storage-efficient. Backwards compatibility: existing ingest paths are unchanged; the new exporter is opt-in via onboard config field "telemetry_export: true". Security: all uploads go through our internal signer and use customer-scoped prefixes for private registries. See linked linear tickets for rollout plan and QA checklist.

release_notes: Onboard telemetry exporter and autodraft release briefs: adds an opt-in telemetry exporter that writes compact JSONL shards for each onboarded model/version; introduces an autodraft release-brief generator that summarizes profile diffs and sampled performance highlights into a markdown draft; UI preview for model reviewers; configurable retention and sampling gates. Impact: opt-in feature, no breaking changes; helps reviewers and release engineers understand deltas faster.
